oewn-04659795-n.learner: the habit of saying little and not telling people more than you have to
examples: It was owing to him, to his reserve and want of proper consideration, that Wickham's character had been so misunderstood

connotation.why: sits among reticence, taciturnity and secretiveness, which differ in how they weigh holding back

oewn-13389225-n.learner: something kept back or saved so that it can be used later or for a special purpose
examples: The country keeps a reserve of oil for emergencies.

oewn-08604729-n.learner: an area of land that is kept for a particular purpose
examples: The birds nest safely inside the nature reserve.

oewn-08223381-n.learner: soldiers who are not on active duty but can be called to serve in an emergency
examples: When the war began, the army called up its reserves.

oewn-10690481-n.learner: a player who plays only when one of the team's starting players is taken off
examples: She sat on the bench as a reserve for most of the season.

oewn-13781913-n.learner: in medicine, the ability the body has in store to respond so that it can keep its life-supporting functions working
examples: Older patients have less heart reserve, so a long operation is riskier for them.

oewn-07520446-n.learner: a feeling of too much concern about someone or something
examples: Elizabeth began to like them herself, when she saw how much affection and solicitude they showed for Jane.
Elizabeth looked at her sister with incredulous solicitude, but said nothing.

connotation.why: the gloss marks the concern as excessive, against plain concern or care

oewn-00826017-a.learner: not feeling safe and secure, or giving no comfort and nothing to make you feel better
examples: The farmers stayed uneasy until the rain finally came.

oewn-02465209-s.learner: causing worry, full of worry, or showing worry
examples: her husband looked impenetrably grave; her daughters, alarmed, anxious, uneasy.
There was an uneasy silence after the news was read out.

oewn-00482429-s.learner: uncomfortable with other people, and unsure and stiff in the way you behave
examples: He was always uneasy with strangers and hardly spoke at parties.

oewn-01928961-a.learner: without rest for the body or mind, or not letting you rest
examples: She fell into an uneasy sleep and woke many times in the night.
I have a warm unguarded temper, and I may perhaps have sometimes spoken my opinion of him, and to him, too freely.

connotation.why: a milder neighbour of hot-tempered and excitable for the same quickness to flare up

oewn-02541266-a.learner: friendly, and ready to respond to other people with feeling
examples: She gave us a warm greeting at the door.
He has a warm personality and makes friends easily.

oewn-02539669-a.learner: having or making a pleasant, comfortable heat, or giving or keeping in heat
examples: Come inside; the kitchen is warm.
She wore a warm coat in the snow.

oewn-00809957-s.learner: full of life, excitement, or disagreement
examples: There was a warm debate about the new plan.

oewn-02542324-a.learner: giving a feeling of heat, said most of all of reds, oranges and yellows when talking about colour
examples: She painted the kitchen in warm yellows and oranges.

oewn-00447342-s.learner: of someone searching or guessing, close to the thing they are looking for
examples: You're getting warm; the key is somewhere in this room.

oewn-01072383-s.learner: made or left only a short time ago
examples: The dogs followed the warm trail into the woods.

oewn-00043985-a.learner: really existing now, and not just something that could be or might be
examples: The actual temperature was much lower than the forecast said.

oewn-01940178-s.learner: existing as a real fact or a real deed
examples: it is rash, I think, to conclude that an actual Mr. Collins was impossible or non-existent at the end of the eighteenth century.

oewn-02470192-s.learner: being or showing the true, real nature of something
examples: She said she did it for the money, but her actual motive was revenge.

oewn-01939967-s.learner: really happening, not acted out or copied
examples: We watched the actual wedding on television, not the practice the day before.

oewn-00669833-s.learner: being or existing right now, at this moment
examples: The ship's actual position is twenty miles south of the island.

oewn-00976399-v.learner: to make something known, or to give out a piece of news
examples: Jane had already written a few lines to her sister, to announce their safe arrival in London
Shall you ever have courage to announce to Lady Catherine what is to befall her?

oewn-00967903-v.learner: to tell something to the public, or to state it officially
examples: The government announced a new tax on Friday.

oewn-00976205-v.learner: to be an early sign of something that is coming
examples: Dark clouds announced the coming storm.

oewn-00977459-v.learner: to say the names of people or things
examples: The butler announced each guest as they came in.

oewn-00625978-n.learner: moving and using your muscles in different ways to stay fit
examples: she resolved soon after breakfast to indulge herself in air and exercise.
Voting is the exercise of a citizen's right.

oewn-00731217-n.learner: a task you do or a problem you solve to build a skill or your understanding
examples: Do the exercises at the end of the chapter.

oewn-00034873-n.learner: an action, often spoken of as pointless and leading to nothing
examples: The whole meeting was an exercise in futility.

connotation.why: the gloss says it is often used negatively of the action it names

oewn-00896250-n.learner: training in a planned way by doing the same thing again and again
examples: The team spent the morning in exercise, running the same play over and over.

oewn-07469062-n.learner: a ceremony with people walking in line and giving speeches, usually called exercises in the plural
examples: Graduation exercises will be held in the main hall.

oewn-01797082-s.learner: just this on its own, with nothing added or changed
examples: the mere stateliness of money and rank she thought she could witness without trepidation.

oewn-01103400-s.learner: being nothing more than what is named
examples: his studying the law was a mere pretence;

connotation.why: belittles what it names, set against plain just or only

oewn-06379324-n.learner: a long made-up piece of writing, not in verse, that usually tells a story
examples: This Swiftian quality appears in the present novel as it appears nowhere else in the character of the immortal, the ineffable Mr. Collins.

oewn-03838605-n.learner: a printed book with its pages fastened together that holds a long made-up story
examples: She left the novel open on the train seat.
She had obtained private intelligence that Mr. Darcy did not wish for cards
She found it difficult to obtain even a word from her beyond a monosyllable.

oewn-00523831-v.learner: to receive a certain kind of treatment that is not a physical thing
examples: The plan obtained wide approval from the council.

oewn-02654604-v.learner: to be valid, to apply, or to be true
examples: These old rules no longer obtain in most schools.
